items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: The interviewee mentions Cannonball Adderley only in response to the interviewer's statement ('Listen to Cannonball Adderley and how he...'). The interviewee does not claim any personal interaction, collaboration, or specific relationship with Adderley, merely acknowledging the reference.

ctx.x: didn’t allow me to make that leap was the music. Because I loved Phil Woods and his playing. Because I loved Paul Desmond. I loved Zoot Sims. And that was like a shield that protected me against falling prey to that kind of thinking, man.

That’s wonderful to hear. And I have, it’s not exactly the same, but my introduction to the black race was through — you know I grew up in a suburb where there was one African American student who was sort of probably bussed in from inner-city Rochester and of course he was on the basketball team. And it was my introduction to another race of people, was really through Cannonball Adderley and Count Basie. So it’s really great to hear that that music can surround this.

And, if you would allow me, because how we language things, how we describe things, is so important. So I would amend what you just said and say the first time you met a particular ethnic group or cultural group, which some called going back some called Negro Americans, to black Americans, to African Americans, would have been that, like I said, race is not real in that sense. So I don’t believe that there is a black race or a white race. In that same piece that I’m talking about, I have a short portion where I…
